sequence_finding.question: Did OI begin rising during the main decline or only after price was already lower?
sequence_finding.answer: On the supplied Coinwise sequence, the visible OI rise begins after the major OI decline has already occurred and while price is already in the lower value area. Later, price sweeps lower and then reclaims while a large short-liquidation burst appears. The correct label remains POST_SELLOFF_OI_REBUILD followed by SWEEP_RECLAIM_WITH_SHORT_SQUEEZE_COMPONENT.
sequence_finding.reason: The reclaim is real price evidence, but OI is not expanding cleanly with it and the displayed -8.62M short-liquidation burst means the rebound may be powered substantially by forced short covering. Fresh-long continuation must be proven by holding reclaimed value and then accepting above higher value references.

assessment.important_learning: Post-selloff OI rebuild alone was not bullish. The later sweep/reclaim improved the long case, but the simultaneous large short-liquidation burst means the first rebound should be classified as squeeze-assisted until price holds reclaimed value and follow-through appears without relying on forced covering.

long_candidate.execution_market: MEXC BTCUSDT perpetual only after checking a fresh synchronized quote
long_candidate.required_trigger: Hold/reclaim the dPOC-area context, avoid immediate loss of the reclaimed zone, and preferably show price follow-through with CVD stabilizing or improving. A breakout above dIVAH should be retested rather than chased.
long_candidate.invalidated_if: Price loses the reclaimed lower-value area and accepts back below it; a renewed loss of the sweep structure reopens the lower-tail scenario.

downside_if_reclaim_fails.note: These are structural references, not automatic buy orders or permission to widen an existing stop.

short_candidate.required_trigger: Failure at 77205/77500 or another reclaimed-lost area with price rolling over and CVD weakening; do not short solely because the squeeze already happened.

data_quality.warning: Do not translate Coinwise levels one-for-one into MEXC orders. Use Coinwise for structure/order-flow context and MEXC for execution only after synchronized confirmation.

learning_summary: Classify OI by timing, not just sign: during the impulse, after the impulse, or during the reclaim.
Post-selloff OI rising + flat CVD + no price reclaim is leverage rebuild, not a long signal.
A later sweep and reclaim can upgrade the long hypothesis, but a large short-liquidation burst means the first rebound may be squeeze-driven rather than fresh-long driven.
If price rises while OI curls lower and short liquidations spike, label the move SHORT_COVERING_DOMINANT_OR_MIXED until follow-through proves otherwise.
Do not chase the first squeeze candle. Prefer a hold/retest of reclaimed value or acceptance above dIVAH with confirmation.
A long edge requires location plus reaction plus confirmation; location alone is insufficient.
Keep execution-market levels separate from analytical-feed levels until basis and timestamps are synchronized.
